mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off sentiment that compresses equity discount rates, lowering expected future cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns within the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 0.25 percentage points within a single month
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in the same month are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (t-test p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed prior quarter median for ≥2 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below the prior 12-month average indicate deflationary pressure, which reduces expected inflation and discount rates, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for 3 consecutive months below its 12-month rolling average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the same period are negative and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05), or CPIAUCSL recovers above the 12-month average within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) above the prior 4-quarter average coincides with stronger consumer demand, strengthening equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns within the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds its 4-quarter moving average by at least 2,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05), or employment growth reverts to trend within 2 months without a follow-on equity rally.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising industrial production (INDPRO) above trend suggest expanding supply capacity, which, when coupled with elevated consumer demand (HOUST), reduces near-term discounting and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: AND: INDPRO > 12-month rolling average AND HOUST increases month-over-month for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.1), or either INDPRO or HOUST fails to meet trend thresholds for ≥3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below the prior 6-month average signals labor market tightening, which raises expected growth and equity risk premia, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below its 6-month moving average by at least 0.2 percentage points in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.1), or UNRATE recovers to the 6-month average within 2 months without equity sell-off.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in manufacturing activity (GDPC1) below the prior 3-quarter average indicates cyclical softening, which reduces growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for 3 consecutive quarters below its 3-quarter moving average
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05), or GDPC1 recovers above the 3-quarter average within 2 quarters.

mechanism_narrative: When the monetary policy rate (FEDFUNDS) remains persistently below its pre-crisis average for 4 consecutive months, it signals accommodative policy sustaining risk asset valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS stays below its pre-Crisis peak (set at 5.25%) for 4 consecutive months
regime_hint: low for extended period (below pre-crisis peak)
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not positive or not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS rises above pre-crisis peak within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in job openings (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) signals a tight labor market, which raises wage growth expectations and can depress equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: AND: PAYEMS increases by ≥10,000 jobs AND UNRATE falls by ≥0.1 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically negative (t-test p > 0.1), or either PAYEMS or UNRATE fails to meet the specified directional change for ≥2 consecutive months.
